Hands-on tutorials for the workshop. Each one is a downloadable `.qmd` file with code, *Think about it* prompts, and collapsible answers — open it in RStudio, point the data paths at your local copy of the dataset (see [Datasets](Datasets.qmd)), and run it chunk by chunk.

::: callout-important
The download links below serve each tutorial as `Tutorial_XX_….qmd.txt`. After saving the file, **drop the trailing `.txt` so the filename ends in `.qmd`** before opening in RStudio. (The `.txt` suffix is a workaround that stops the browser from trying to render the source as a webpage.)
:::

## Core tutorial series — laptop path (`ifnb` + `stxBrain`)

Tutorials 01–08 use the **`ifnb`** dataset (Kang *et al.* 2017): \~14k cells across two samples (CTRL and IFN-β–stimulated PBMCs), \~25 MB, installed via `SeuratData::InstallData("ifnb")`. Tutorial 11 uses **`stxBrain`** (10x Visium mouse brain, two sections), \~50 MB, installed via `SeuratData::InstallData("stxBrain")`. Tutorial 05 also uses the bulk `airway` dataset that ships with the `airway` Bioconductor package (Part A of that tutorial). Tutorials 09 (scATAC) and 10 (WGCNA) have their own datasets — see [Datasets](Datasets.qmd). The whole sequence runs comfortably on a laptop.

## Talapas Advanced — HPC path (raw FASTQ → differential abundance) {#talapas-advanced}

The Talapas Advanced series mirrors the laptop workflow, but runs it on the **University of Oregon's Talapas HPC cluster** with **SLURM batch jobs**, starting from **raw FASTQs** rather than the pre-computed counts matrix. The dataset is the **20k NSCLC DTC** sample from 10x Genomics — \~250 MB filtered, 7 donors, 3' v3.1 multiplex.

Each row gives you the **HTML** to read in your browser, the **`.qmd` source** (with `eval = F`, the way the laptop tutorials are distributed), and an **executable script** (R / Python / bash) that you can submit directly to SLURM. The `.qmd` is where the prose explanation lives; the executable script is what you actually run on the cluster, with minimal comments.

::: callout-tip
**Workflow.** Each Talapas tutorial uses the output of the previous one (an `.rds` written to `/projects/<PIRG>/<user>/nsclc/objects/`), so they form a single pipeline. You can submit them one at a time, or chain them with SLURM job dependencies (`--dependency=afterok:<JOBID>`).
:::

## Datasets used

Full dataset descriptions, install / download instructions, and a disk-space budget live on the **[Datasets](Datasets.qmd)** page.

Primary sources:

-   **scRNA-seq (laptop, Tutorials 01–04 + 05B + 06–08)** — [`ifnb`](https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/integration_introduction.html) via `SeuratData::InstallData("ifnb")` (Kang *et al.* 2017, \~25 MB)
-   **DESeq2 primer (Tutorial 05, Part A)** — `airway` Bioconductor package (no manual download)
-   **scRNA-seq (Talapas Advanced)** — [10x Genomics: 20k NSCLC DTC, 3' v3.1 Multiplex](https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/20-k-mixture-of-nsclc-dt-cs-from-7-donors-3-v-3-1-multiplex-3-1-standard-6-0-0) (raw FASTQs and/or **filtered** matrix — \~250 MB)
-   **scATAC-seq (Tutorial 09)** — [10x Genomics: PBMC 10k scATAC-seq v1](https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/10-k-peripheral-blood-mononuclear-cells-pbm-cs-from-a-healthy-donor-1-standard-1-1-0)
-   **WGCNA (Tutorial 10)** — [GEO: GSE152418 (COVID-19 PBMC bulk RNA-seq)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE152418)
-   **Spatial transcriptomics (Tutorial 11)** — `stxBrain` (10x Visium adult mouse brain, anterior + posterior sections) via `SeuratData::InstallData("stxBrain")` (\~50 MB)

By convention the tutorials read from `../data/` (i.e. a `data/` folder at the repository root). For the `ifnb`-based laptop tutorials there's nothing to put in `data/` to start — the package handles the download. Place 10x downloads there or adjust the paths in the `Read10X*` calls.

## Adapted from

-   The `ifnb` workflow (Tutorials 01–04) follows the official [Seurat integration tutorial](https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/integration_introduction.html), with workshop-specific commentary, *Think about it* prompts, and a four-tutorial pacing.
-   Tutorial 05 (DESeq2) follows the worked examples in [Khushbu Patel's YouTube Tutorials repo](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials).
-   Pedagogical inspiration on QC pacing, marker plot ordering, and integration diagnostics: [scNotebooks](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/) (Sengupta lab).
-   The Talapas Advanced track follows Patel's `singleCell_standard_workflow.R` on the 20k NSCLC dataset, ported to SLURM batch scripts.
